El Nino/Southern Oscillation (ENSO) Diagnostic Discussion
NWS Climate Prediction Center College Park MD
900 AM EDT Thu 12 Nov 2026

NOTE: figures mentioned in the discussion are available on
the internet at HTTP://WWW.CPC.NCEP.NOAA.GOV

ENSO Alert System Status: El Nino Advisory

Synopsis: El Nino continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very
strong El Nino likely through January-March 2027 (remaining
greater than a 79percent chance).

Compared to last month, El Nino strengthened as sea surface
temperature anomalies exceeded 4.0degC, extending farther
westward across the eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean
(Fig. 1). The Nino indices increased, reaching +2.5degC
in Nino-3.4, +3.6degC in Nino-3, and +4.4degC in Nino-1+2
(Fig. 2). The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average
from 180deg-100degW) remained significantly above average
(Fig. 3), associated with a deeper-than-average thermocline and
anomalies exceeding +10.0degC at depth in the eastern Pacific
Ocean (Fig. 4). Low-level westerly and upper-level easterly
wind anomalies extended from the western to the east-central
equatorial Pacific. Convection and rainfall remained enhanced
from the central to the eastern Pacific, while suppressed
conditions persisted over Indonesia (Fig. 5). The traditional
and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were consistently
negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system
reflected the ongoing evolution of El Nino.

The CPC Official ENSO outlook, which synthesizes multiple
models from North America and abroad, indicates El Nino will
continue to strengthen before beginning to weaken in early 2027
(Figs. 6-8). Chances for a historic event exceeding previous
El Ninos dating back to 1950 (+2.5degC or more for a 3-month
RONI value) are now ~60percent for the October-December
and November-January periods, remaining at better than
even odds. Even with a very strong El Nino, the chances of
experiencing impacts consistent with El Nino are higher, though
not guaranteed (see CPC outlooks for probabilities of seasonal
anomalies). In summary, El Nino continues to strengthen, with
a strong-to-very strong El Nino likely through January-March
2027 (remaining greater than a 79percent chance).

This discussion is a consolidated effort of the National Oceanic
and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), NOAA's National Weather
Service, and their funded institutions. Oceanic and atmospheric
conditions are updated weekly on the Climate Prediction
Center website (El Nino/La Nina Current Conditions and Expert
Discussions). A probabilistic strength forecast is available
here. The next ENSO Diagnostics Discussion is scheduled for
10 December 2026. To receive an e-mail notification when the
monthly ENSO Diagnostic Discussions are released, please send
an e-mail message to: ncep.list.enso-update@noaa.gov.
